types.name: ledger.read.v1.BalanceUpdate
types.doc:
BalanceUpdate is one publication on an account's balance stream.

 A TRADING update is one step of the account's Trading balances, at a
 position (trading_epoch, trading_sequence). Within an epoch the sequence
 runs 1, 2, 3 with no gap. A new epoch starts again at 1, and its updates
 up to its first complete one carry every asset the account holds in
 Trading.

 A FUNDING update carries one asset's Funding balance. It is not sequenced:
 a higher funding_revision is newer. Its trading_epoch and trading_sequence
 are unset: tell the two kinds apart by account, never by a zero epoch.

 Keep the balances exact as follows:

 1. Subscribe to the stream and buffer its updates.
 2. Call GetBalances and apply its balances. Its position (E, Q) is
    (trading_epoch, trading_sequence). If it answers unavailable, retry it
    with a backoff.
 3. Drop buffered and later TRADING updates of epoch E with a sequence at or
    below Q; a reconnect can repeat one. Apply E's sequences Q + 1, Q + 2,
    and so on, in order.
 4. Keep a dropped set of epochs: every epoch you held before E, and every
    epoch other than E of an update received before the GetBalances call
    that answered E began. GetBalances never answers a dropped epoch again,
    so drop a TRADING update of a dropped epoch without reloading: after a
    move, the earlier epoch's late updates can still arrive. Reload, from
    step 2, when:
    - a TRADING update's epoch is neither E nor dropped, including one
      buffered while the call ran: the numbering restarted;
    - its sequence skips a number: an update was missed;
    - after an incomplete update of E, E's next sequence does not arrive
      within 2 seconds. FUNDING updates, repeats and updates of dropped
      epochs do not stop the timer;
    - the subscription reports that missed publications could not be
      recovered.
 5. Apply a FUNDING update when its funding_revision is higher than the one
    held for its asset.

 GetBalances reflects every balance update published before the call began,
 so a reload covers anything the subscription missed in the answer's epoch,
 even a final update of an idle account, and an earlier epoch's Trading
 transfers as below. Show Trading values after an update with complete set:
 in between, the same step continues in the next update.

 After a move, a new epoch's Trading values can be older than the previous
 epoch's last ones: its owner may not have applied the latest transfers yet.
 Until its trading_applied_through_ts_ns reaches the last one you saw, the
 epoch is catching up, and its later updates apply those transfers.
 GetBalances waits, or fails with UNAVAILABLE, rather than answer such a
 cut below a Trading transfer the stream published in an earlier epoch,
 including one you never received. Right after a server restart it may not
 know every such transfer, so still count a transfer as applied only by a
 receipt in the current epoch: its leg, or a trading_applied_through_ts_ns
 at or past its ts_ns.

fields.name: account
fields.doc: TRADING or FUNDING: which balances this update carries.

fields.name: trading_epoch
fields.doc:
TRADING only. The Trading numbering this update is in, as GetBalances
 returns it. It changes when the numbering restarts: drop an update of a
 dropped epoch, and reload on any other epoch than the current one
 (step 4). Compare it only for equality; its value has no order.

fields.name: trading_sequence
fields.doc: TRADING only. This update's place in its epoch, from 1, with no gap.

fields.name: complete
fields.doc:
TRADING only. True when the account's Trading values are a consistent
 snapshot after this update; false while the same step continues in the
 next update.

fields.name: balances
fields.doc:
The assets this update changed, each at most once. A TRADING update sets
 trading, reserved and available; a FUNDING update sets funding and
 funding_revision. The other kind's fields are unset.

fields.name: transfers
fields.doc:
TRADING only. The Trading transfer legs this update applied, oldest
 first. Each sets asset_id, amount_e18, transfer_code, account_code,
 ts_us, ts_ns, balance_after_e18, is_debit and transfer_id; link_id,
 flow_id, source and destination are unset here and are published on the
 transfer stream and by ListTransfers. After a move, a transfer's legs
 can arrive again in the new epoch: (transfer_id, is_debit) identifies a
 leg.

fields.name: trading_applied_through_ts_ns
fields.doc:
TRADING only. Every Trading transfer of the account whose ts_ns is at or
 below this value is applied in this update's balances, whether or not its
 leg was received. It is a receipt within trading_epoch. While a transfer
 of the account could not be applied, this value stays below it, until a
 later balance of that asset includes it; it never passes a transfer that
 is not applied. Nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).

types.name: ledger.read.v1.CreateStatementExportRequest
types.doc:
CreateStatementExportRequest asks for a whole-period account statement,
 ledger or balances file of one account. The period is at most 366 days long; a longer or empty
 period is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

fields.name: subaccount_id
fields.doc:
Optional public subaccount ID. When omitted, subaccount-scoped API keys
 use their bound subaccount; other callers use their authenticated root
 account. The statement covers that one account only.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc:
Start of the statement period (UTC), inclusive: after
 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and no later than the request.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc:
End of the statement period (UTC), exclusive, by
 2262-04-11T23:47:16Z. A period still open when the export is created
 ends at that instant; see StatementExport.complete_through.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.doc:
Optional public unified asset ID. When unset/0, the statement covers
 every asset; an ID that names no asset is refused.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc:
Client-chosen key, 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `.`, `_`,
 `:` or `-`, unique per root account. Repeating a request with the same
 key returns the same export; the same key with different request fields
 is refused.

fields.name: type
fields.doc:
Kind of file to produce; required. Every type has the same period,
 asset filter, limits and lifecycle; a BALANCES period must also start
 inside the account history.

ErrorCode enumerates stable machine-readable error codes for the Ledger Read
 API. These mirror the REST problem+json "code" field for parity between REST
 and ConnectRPC clients.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_MISSING_ACCOUNT_ID
values.doc: Missing or invalid account identifier (legacy; used by older endpoints).

values.name: ERROR_CODE_MISSING_WALLET
values.doc: Wallet-specific errors for balance lookups by wallet.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_UPSTREAM_ERROR
values.doc:
Ledger data needed to answer the request is temporarily unavailable.
 Retry later.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_INVALID_SUBACCOUNT_ID
values.doc: subaccount_id is zero or not an encoded public subaccount identifier.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED
values.doc: The idempotency key was used for a request with other fields.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_LIMIT_REACHED
values.doc:
The root account already has the most statement exports queued or being
 produced; wait for one to finish.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_READY
values.doc: The statement export's file is not ready yet.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_EXPIRED

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILED
values.doc: The statement export failed and has no file.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_CANCELABLE

The statement export already finished, READY, FAILED or EXPIRED, so it
 can no longer be canceled.

values.name: ERROR_CODE_STATEMENT_EXPORT_CANCELED

 balances the account history holds; ErrorDetail.history_available_from

types.name: ledger.read.v1.GetBalancesResponse
types.doc:
GetBalancesResponse is the account's balances with the position of its
 Trading values.

 The Trading values of every asset are one atomic cut: all are taken at the
 single position (trading_epoch, trading_sequence) the response names, never
 a mix of two positions, and never at a position older than one the balance
 stream already published. The Funding values carry their own
 funding_revision and are not part of that position.

fields.name: balances
fields.doc:
One entry for every supported unified asset, including assets with zero
 balances. Sorted by available trading amount (highest first), then by
 asset symbol alphabetically.

fields.name: trading_epoch
fields.doc:
The Trading numbering the balances' Trading values are in. It changes
 when the numbering restarts: then reload. Compare it only for equality;
 its value has no order. Zero, with trading_sequence zero, when the
 account has no Trading balances yet.

fields.name: trading_sequence
fields.doc:
The Trading sequence the balances' Trading values are at, within
 trading_epoch: apply the balance stream's Trading updates from
 trading_sequence + 1 on (see BalanceUpdate).

fields.name: trading_applied_through_ts_ns
fields.doc:
Every Trading transfer of the account whose ts_ns is at or below this
 value is applied in these balances, a receipt within trading_epoch.
 While a transfer of the account could not be applied, this value stays
 below it, until a later balance of that asset includes it; it never
 passes a transfer that is not applied. Nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).

types.name: ledger.read.v1.StatementExport
types.doc:
StatementExport is a whole-period account statement, ledger or balances
 file produced in the background as one CSV file.

 The file is RFC 4180 CSV in UTF-8 with CRLF line endings: the header row,
 then the rows of the period up to complete_through. ACCOUNT_STATEMENT and
 LEDGER rows come oldest first, and a period without movements yields the
 header row alone. Every type reads the same ledger movements of the
 account; type sets the file's rows and columns.

 An ACCOUNT_STATEMENT row is the effect of one entry on one account bucket
 in one asset. An entry is one ledger operation, such as a trade with its
 fees, a deposit, a withdrawal step or an internal transfer.

 ACCOUNT_STATEMENT columns, in order:
 - `time`: entry time, RFC 3339 in UTC with microseconds, for example
   `2026-11-12T19:52:07.734123Z`.
 - `entry_id`: entry identifier, an unsigned 128-bit integer as a decimal
   string. It is the `transfer_id` of the entry's first transfer leg on the
   account within the export's period, as LedgerReadService.ListTransfers
   returns it, and is the same whichever asset the export is limited to. A
   period boundary can fall between the legs of one entry: each export then
   holds its own part of the entry, under the `transfer_id` of that part's
   first leg, so do not join rows across periods on `entry_id` alone.
 - `type`: `trade` for a trade's settlement and its fees; otherwise the
   entry's transfer reason, such as `deposit`, `withdraw`,
   `internal_transfer`, `funding_to_trading` or `system_adjustment`.
 - `account`: account bucket, `funding` or `trading`.
 - `asset`: asset symbol.
 - `amount`: signed balance change of the entry in whole units of the
   asset, excluding the fees in `fee`, for example `-5000` or `0.1`. Fees
   the account receives are included here.
 - `fee`: fees the account paid in the asset for the entry, in whole units
   of the asset; `0` when none.
 - `balance`: account bucket balance in the asset after the entry, in whole
   units of the asset. For consecutive rows of the same bucket and asset,
   each balance equals the previous balance plus `amount` minus `fee`.
 - `link_id`: correlation ID shared by related transfer legs, the trade's
   match ID for trades; empty when unavailable.
 - `flow_id`: public lifecycle flow ID when the entry belongs to a chain
   lifecycle flow, such as a deposit, a withdrawal or an internal transfer,
   linked before the export was created; empty otherwise. A flow linked
   later, which LedgerReadService.ListTransfers then shows, is not in the
   file: a new export shows it.

 A LEDGER row is one ledger movement: one transfer leg on the account,
 as LedgerReadService.ListTransfers returns it. A trade's settlement is
 several rows, such as its base and quote legs and each fee.

 LEDGER columns, in order:
 - `time`: transfer time, RFC 3339 in UTC with microseconds.
 - `transfer_id`: transfer identifier, an unsigned 128-bit integer as a
   decimal string, as LedgerReadService.ListTransfers returns it. With
   `account` and `side` it identifies the row.
 - `account`: account bucket, `funding` or `trading`.
 - `asset`: asset symbol.
 - `type`: transfer reason, such as `trade_base`, `trade_quote`,
   `maker_fee`, `taker_fee`, `rebate`, `deposit`, `withdraw`,
   `internal_transfer` or `funding_to_trading`.
 - `side`: `debit` when the movement takes from the account bucket,
   `credit` when it adds to it.
 - `amount`: signed balance change in whole units of the asset: negative
   for a debit, positive for a credit.
 - `counterparty`: kind of the transfer's other side: `funding_account`,
   `trading_account`, `external_address`, `private_counterparty`,
   `fee_account` or `system_account`; empty when unknown.
 - `balance`: account bucket balance in the asset after the movement, in
   whole units of the asset. For consecutive rows of the same bucket and
   asset, each balance equals the previous balance plus `amount`.
 - `link_id`: correlation ID shared by related transfer legs, the trade's
   match ID for trades; empty when unavailable.
 - `flow_id`: public lifecycle flow ID when the transfer belongs to a chain
   lifecycle flow linked before the export was created; empty otherwise,
   as for `flow_id` of an account statement.

 A BALANCES row is one account bucket in one asset over the period: its
 balance at start_time, the period's ledger movements on it, and its
 balance at complete_through. Rows come sorted by `account`, then `asset`.
 A bucket and asset with a zero balance at both ends and no movement has no
 row, so an account without any yields the header row alone. The period
 must start at or after the earliest instant whose balances the account
 history holds: an earlier start is refused when the export is created
 (CreateStatementExport) and fails the export if that instant moves later
 before the file is produced.

 BALANCES columns, in order:
 - `account`: account bucket, `funding` or `trading`.
 - `asset`: asset symbol.
 - `opening_balance`: balance of the bucket in the asset at start_time.
 - `credits`: total the period's movements added to the bucket, the sum of
   the LEDGER file's credit rows of that bucket and asset; `0` when none.
 - `debits`: total the period's movements took from the bucket, the sum of
   the LEDGER file's debit rows of that bucket and asset, as a positive
   amount; `0` when none.
 - `closing_balance`: balance of the bucket in the asset at
   complete_through. Every row reconciles: `closing_balance` equals
   `opening_balance` plus `credits` minus `debits`.
 - `movements`: number of the period's ledger movements on the bucket in
   the asset.

 Amounts are exact decimal strings with up to 18 fractional digits and no
 trailing zeros.

 A READY file downloads in one of two ways:
 - StatementExportService.GetStatementExportDownloadUrl returns a URL valid
   for 60 seconds from signing that needs no credentials, so a browser can
   save the file straight to disk.
 - An authenticated `GET /v1/statements/exports/{exportId}/file` returns the
   file as `text/csv` and supports HTTP `Range` requests.

 Both save the file as `account-statement-<exportId>.csv`,
 `ledger-<exportId>.csv` or `balances-<exportId>.csv`, by type. Before the file is READY
 both answer FAILED_PRECONDITION with STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_READY, REST
 `409 Conflict`; a FAILED export answers STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILED, REST `409`;
 an EXPIRED export, or a file already deleted, answers
 STATEMENT_EXPORT_EXPIRED, REST `410 Gone`, and so does a download URL
 request for a file with less than 5 seconds left; a CANCELED export
 answers STATEMENT_EXPORT_CANCELED, REST `409`. REST errors are
 `application/problem+json` whose `code` is the ErrorCode name, such as
 `STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_READY`: `401` without valid credentials, `403
 PERMISSION_DENIED` for an API key without READ_STATEMENTS, `404 NOT_FOUND`
 for an export the caller cannot read, and `503 UPSTREAM_ERROR`, with
 `Retry-After`, when the request can be retried.

 An export belongs to the root account whose session or API key created it.
 Any session or API key of that root that may read the export's account can
 read and download it, whichever of them created it. A member of a
 subaccount shared from another root sees only the exports its own root
 created, and the subaccount's owner does not see those: an export of
 another root, or of an account the caller can no longer read, answers
 NOT_FOUND, as one that does not exist.

fields.name: export_id
fields.doc:
Public ID of the export.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: subaccount_id
fields.doc:
Public subaccount ID of the account the statement covers; unset for a
 root account.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: Start of the statement period (UTC), inclusive.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: End of the requested statement period (UTC), exclusive.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.doc: Public unified asset ID the statement is limited to; 0 for every asset.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc: Idempotency key of the request that created the export.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where the export is.

fields.name: complete_through
fields.doc:
End of what the file covers (UTC), exclusive: the earlier of end_time and
 the instant the export was created. Every movement recorded before the
 export was created and before complete_through is in the file.

fields.name: movements
fields.doc:
Ledger movements written to the file so far; the file's total when
 READY.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: Bytes written to the file so far; the file's size when READY.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the export was created.

fields.name: ready_at
fields.doc: When the file became READY; unset before.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When a READY file expires, 7 days after ready_at; unset before READY.

fields.name: failure_reason
fields.doc: Why the export FAILED; unspecified otherwise.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: Kind of file the export produces, as requested.

fields.name: history_available_from
fields.doc:
Earliest instant whose balances the account history holds, which a
 BALANCES export's period must start at or after. Set only when
 failure_reason is STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILURE_REASON_HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.StatementExportFailureReason
types.doc: StatementExportFailureReason is why a statement export failed.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILURE_REASON_TOO_LARGE
values.doc:
The period holds more than 4,000,000 ledger movements of the account,
 the most one export reads. Every asset's movements count, even for an
 export limited to one asset: an entry is built from all of its ledger
 operation's movements before the asset's rows are selected. Split the
 period into shorter exports.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILURE_REASON_UNAVAILABLE
values.doc: The file could not be produced in time. Create a new export.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILURE_REASON_HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE
values.doc:
A BALANCES export's period starts before the earliest instant whose
 balances the account history holds, which moved later after the export
 was created. history_available_from is that instant: create a new
 export that starts at or after it.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.StatementExportStatus
types.doc: StatementExportStatus is where a statement export is.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_QUEUED
values.doc:
Accepted. The export waits until the account history covers its period
 and no other export of the account is being produced.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_PROCESSING
values.doc: The file is being produced; movements and bytes count its progress.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_READY
values.doc: The file is complete and can be downloaded until expires_at.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_FAILED
values.doc: The file could not be produced; failure_reason says why.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_EXPIRED
values.doc: The file was deleted at expires_at; create a new export for it.

values.name: STATEMENT_EXPORT_STATUS_CANCELED
values.doc:
Canceled with CancelStatementExport before it finished. It has no file
 and no longer counts toward the root account's exports in progress.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.StatementExportType
types.doc: StatementExportType is the kind of file a statement export produces.

values.name: ACCOUNT_STATEMENT
values.doc:
Account statement: one row per entry, account bucket and asset, with the
 entry's net amount, the fees paid and the balance after it.

values.name: LEDGER
values.doc:
Ledger: one row per ledger movement, each transfer leg on its own, with
 its transfer reason, side, counterparty and the balance after it.

values.name: BALANCES
values.doc:
Balances: one row per account bucket and asset, with its balance at the
 start and at the end of the period and the period's credits and debits.
 Its period must start inside the account history; see
 StatementExport.history_available_from.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.TransferRow
types.doc: TransferRow describes one debit or credit leg of a ledger transfer.

fields.name: asset_id
fields.doc:
Public unified asset ID. Resolve its symbol through the spot configuration
 API. U128 amounts in this row always use a fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.

fields.name: amount_e18
fields.doc: Transfer amount at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.

fields.name: transfer_code
fields.doc: Product reason for this transfer.

fields.name: account_code
fields.doc: Account bucket affected by this transfer.

fields.name: ts_us
fields.doc: Transfer timestamp in microseconds since epoch (UTC).

fields.name: balance_after_e18
fields.doc: Post-transfer balance at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.

fields.name: is_debit
fields.doc: True when this row is the debit leg; false when it is the credit leg.

fields.name: link_id
fields.doc: Correlation ID used to group related transfer legs. Zero when unavailable.

fields.name: flow_id
fields.doc: Public lifecycle flow ID when this transfer belongs to a chain lifecycle flow.

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
Debit side of the transfer. This relationship is debit-to-credit rather
 than row-relative; use is_debit to determine whether this row is the debit leg.

fields.name: destination
fields.doc:
Credit side of the transfer. This relationship is debit-to-credit rather
 than row-relative; use is_debit to determine whether this row is the credit leg.

fields.name: transfer_id
fields.doc:
Stable transfer identifier, an unsigned 128-bit integer as a decimal
 string. Both legs of a transfer share it; with account_code and is_debit
 it identifies this row.

fields.name: ts_ns
fields.doc:
Exact transfer timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC); ts_us is this
 value divided by 1,000, rounded down. Compare it with a balance update's
 trading_applied_through_ts_ns.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.TransferRowBatch
types.doc:
TransferRowBatch is one realtime publication on an account's transfer
 stream: every transfer leg queued for the stream when it was sent, at most
 256 and at most 64 KiB. Legs arrive in the order the account's transfers
 settled, except that a leg of a deposit or withdrawal still waiting for its
 lifecycle details arrives once they are known.

 (transfer_id, account_code, is_debit) identifies a leg. Apply legs in array
 order and in publication order; a leg whose identity was already received
 replaces the earlier copy, for example when the leg is published again with
 its flow_id. When the subscription reports that missed publications could
 not be recovered, reload recent transfers over REST.

fields.name: events
fields.doc: Transfer legs, oldest first. At least one leg.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.TransferSide
types.doc: TransferSide describes one side of a ledger transfer for display.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Display classification for this transfer side.

fields.name: account_id
fields.doc:
Public root account or subaccount ID when this side is safe to identify. Never
 populated for private counterparties or non-user ledger accounts.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: address
fields.doc:
Address for this side when known. For EXTERNAL_ADDRESS this is an
 external-chain wallet address from lifecycle correlation; for identifiable
 Polyester accounts this is a Polyester smart-account address.
 May be empty until the corresponding lifecycle details are available.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.doc:
PolyChain-registered external network identifier for EXTERNAL_ADDRESS.
 This matches chain.zipper.v1.ChainConfig.chain_id and is not the chain's
 native identifier (for example, an EIP-155 id) or the Polyester chain id.

types.name: ledger.read.v1.TransferSideKind
types.doc: TransferSideKind identifies the display class for one side of a transfer.

values.name: FUNDING_ACCOUNT
values.doc: Polyester funding account.

values.name: TRADING_ACCOUNT
values.doc: Polyester trading account.

values.name: EXTERNAL_ADDRESS
values.doc:
External wallet or chain address. The address is lifecycle-derived and may
 be empty until ledger-to-lifecycle correlation is projected.

values.name: PRIVATE_COUNTERPARTY
values.doc:
Private off-chain counterparty that must not be identified to the caller.
 account_id and address are intentionally omitted.

values.name: FEE_ACCOUNT
values.doc: Fee ledger side, for example spot or perp trading fees.

values.name: SYSTEM_ACCOUNT
values.doc: System, operator, clearing, or other non-user side.
